counter_reasons: Which file:line shows the problem? appendActions (lib.mjs:683-708) has no uniqueness check, and finalizeAction (lib.mjs:243-256) makes action_id a pure function of content plus the batch-wide `now`. replay (lib.mjs:302-308) rejects the duplicate. The critic's lib.mjs line numbers are off by roughly 1-8 lines because of drift in the working tree. The functions and the behaviour are as described, so this does not refute the claim.

Is this a stated rule or only a preference? It breaks the store's own contract: replay says ids must be unique, and records are immutable. writeRecords already enforces in-batch uniqueness through its `known` map and appendActions does not, which is a consistency/DRY gap. The project rule 'Do not hide failing tests' also applies, because the result is a red contract test on the committed store that cannot be fixed inside policy.

What concrete failure follows? I reproduced it end to end on a scratch copy of the store. The writer reports success (exit 0, stored:true twice), then `pnpm trace lint` fails with exit 1. Later appends keep succeeding, so nothing flags the problem until lint or vitest runs. contracts.test.mjs:116 would then fail on the default store.

Can the trigger actually happen? Dedup in critic-panel.js:226-240 is keyed on severity plus the exact title. Two critics whose wording differs, or the same title raised at blocker and at important, can both set revisits to the same prior record as still-present on an identical tree. That produces two identical REUSE drafts. The trigger is plausible, not hypothetical.

Is it really irrecoverable? Within the declared policy (trace.md:17-20, no hand edits, corrections only through revising records), yes: no record can remove a duplicate action line, and rotateStore moves lines without removing them. Outside policy, an uncommitted store could be restored with git, or the line deleted by hand. That is a policy exception, not a supported recovery path, so the word holds in the policy sense.

Is the recommendation proportionate? Yes. Tracking seen action_ids (prior plus in-batch) in appendActions mirrors the existing writeRecords pattern. Deduping reuseActions by record_id in critic-panel stops a fail-closed batch from dropping the one legitimate REUSE. A unit test with two identical drafts covers the gap. lib.test.mjs has no such test today.

The only inaccuracy is drift in the critic's lib.mjs line numbers, which does not affect the claim.

Lines 285 and 318 then keep only the skeptic's type. Line 178 and the prompt at 275 invite the retype. Refutation failed: the cited lines say what the critic claims.

CQ2, rule or preference: this breaks a stated rule, not a style preference. trace.md defines the gate as deterministic rung discipline ('no claim stronger than its evidence'; 'reading code is not a measurement'), and the Performance lens (line 137) says 'never estimate'. A retype gets around that backstop, and the backstop exists precisely because the LLM checker is not trusted on this point. Only the retype path weakens the gate; the gate code itself is correct (control run B downgrades as expected).

CQ3, concrete failure: reproduced by running the real workflow body with stub agents. Without the retype it would be defer. The record then licenses CLEAR/HOLD action. Through verdict reuse (lines 256-260) it is carried forward on identical trees. storeMetrics byType and the gate-downgrade counts under-report. lib.mjs semanticViolations accepts the stored record, so neither the workflow nor `pnpm trace write` flags it.

Attempted refutation, 'retyping is legitimate': a critic can over-type a claim (e.g. factual typed as measured), so retyping has a valid use. That does not save the claim. Nothing records the retype, and nothing bounds its direction. The cost of a monotone gate is only an occasional fail-safe defer or qualify, and the skeptic can still return revise with a restated claim in repair.

Attempted refutation, 'a strong-tier skeptic would not do this': it depends on model behaviour, but the gate exists so as not to rely on that. The stub run shows the deterministic path accepts it, which is what the causal claim needs.

Alternatively, always gate under the critic's type t. Put the wrapper at line 281, outside the byte-identical <trace-evidence-gate> block, so the drift test in contracts.test.mjs still passes. Keeping the original type as a record field needs a schema-v1 change (additionalProperties:false), possibly with a policy-version bump. Pushing 'claim-retyped:<from>-><to>' into failed_gates needs no schema change.

claim_text: improve-skills and scan-docs `accept` verdicts never face the evidence gate, and their records carry evidence the workflow fabricates; improve-skills also files `normative` where trace.md says `practical`
subject: the uncommitted TRACE-lite change set (see `git status` / `git diff`): scripts/trace/{lib,cli,bench-judge}.mjs and their tests, .claude/trace/schema-v1.json, the typed-verdict changes in .claude/workf

evidence.result: Only critic-panel.js, loop-iteration.js and trace-bench.js carry the gate. improve-skills.js and scan-docs.js have 0 references to applyEvidenceGate or evidenceChecked.
The test asserts the carrier set is exactly [critic-panel, loop-iteration, trace-bench]. The critic cited line 52, which is off by 7; the content matches.
VERDICT_SCHEMA has only real/editSafe/saferEdit/missing/reason, with no evidence field. traceVerdict returns 'accept' whenever real is true and editSafe is true.
claim_type is hard-coded to 'normative'. The workflow writes {kind:'rule', ref:<lens label>} and {kind:'file_line', ref:<finding's file, no line>}; the verifier returned neither.
storyVerdict returns 'accept' when final === proposed. Every record gets a {kind:'command', ref:'repo code + test search (scan-docs evidence agent)'} item that no command in the workflow produced.

Policy says a checker's accept is downgraded deterministically when its evidence is weaker than the claim type demands. The table lists 'practical | apply this diff (loop-iteration, improve-skills edits) | diff | defer'.
The write-time semanticViolations only checks that the cited evidence kinds intersect acceptNeeds. Because the workflows add rule, file_line and command items themselves, the write-time check passes.

Only contracts.test.mjs:83 mentions them, and it only checks that traceRecords exists. No test checks claim_type or evidence provenance for these workflows.

evidence.ref: critic (frontend-arch): Only critic-panel, loop-iteration and trace-bench carry the gate block (contracts.test.mjs:52). improve-skills derives accept from two booleans (traceVerdict, improve-skills.js:98), and its VERDICT_SCHEMA has no evidence field. It then writes `{kind:'rule', ref:<critic lens label>}` and `{kind:'file_line', ref:<file>}` itself (improve-skills.js:208-214). scan-docs derives accept from `final === pr

counter_reasons: Which file:line shows the problem? improve-skills.js:98-103 makes accept from two booleans with no evidence. improve-skills.js:208-214 hard-codes 'normative' and adds rule and file_line items itself. scan-docs.js:71 makes accept from proposed===final, and scan-docs.js:134 adds a command item no command produced. The only line-number error is contracts.test.mjs:52, which should be :59; the content matches.

Does the write-time check in writeRecords/semanticViolations already enforce the gate, which would refute the finding? No. It only checks which evidence kinds a record cites. Because the workflows add items of the accepted kinds themselves, every accept passes. My harness confirmed validation:'pass' and stored:true for both cases.

Is it only a preference? No. It breaks a stated policy: trace.md:35-36 says a checker's accept is downgraded deterministically when its evidence is weaker than the claim type demands, and trace.md:47 names improve-skills edits as claim type 'practical' needing 'diff'. The code files them as 'normative', which no test catches. It also undercuts the record guarantees in trace.md, since records 'carry evidence' the checker never cited.

Is the harm limited by other gates? Partly, for improve-skills: its command requires user confirmation before applying an edit (improve-skills.md:42-58), so a falsely accepted record still needs a human before CLEAR. scan-docs has no such step. Its accept record licenses the COMMIT of a story status (trace.md:75) and is cited in the story file, so 'E2E tested' with no implementation and no E2E evidence could become a documented status backed by a valid-looking record. That requires both LLM agents to overclaim, which is exactly what the deterministic gate exists to catch.

Are all the evidence items fabricated? Not all of them. In scan-docs, the file_line items come from the maker's implementationFiles, so they are real agent output, though the verifier never confirmed them. In improve-skills, the 'reading' item is the critic's own evidence. The synthesized items are the improve-skills 'rule' (a lens label, not a rule), the improve-skills 'file_line' (a bare file path, no line), and the scan-docs 'command'. The finding names exactly these, so it holds.

Is the recommendation sound and bounded? Yes. Adding evidenceChecked to the verifier schema and running the inlined gate matches how critic-panel and loop-iteration already work, and the carrier test would need updating. Switching improve-skills to 'practical' would put every edit at defer unless the proposed edit is expressed as a diff, so the change has to carry the diff along. The alternative of documenting these two workflows as gate-exempt is also a valid fix. The finding is scoped correctly as important, not blocker.
reason: I verified every substantive part of the finding against the code and reproduced its harness results by running the real workflow bodies with mocked agents. Neither improve-skills.js nor scan-docs.js runs the evidence gate. Both add evidence items the checker never returned: improve-skills adds rule=<lens label> and file_line=<bare file>, and scan-docs adds command='repo code + test search'. Both turn agreement or booleans into accept. As a result, an accept with no real evidence passes the write-time check in writeRecords (validation:'pass', stored:true). The same accept, run through applyEvidenceGate as a normative claim, comes out as defer. improve-skills.js:208 writes 'normative' while trace.md:47 says improve-skills edits are 'practical' needing a diff, and no test checks this. The only error is a minor line reference: the carrier assertion is contracts.test.mjs:59, not :52. The human confirmation step in improve-skills limits harm there, but scan-docs has no such step before a story status is committed.

Is the check 'vacuous in real use'? Refuted. My probes B, C and D show the duplicate-id check catching real cases: identical drafts in one batch (they share `now`), a draft that supplies an existing record_id to shadow or overwrite it, which is the actual immutability guarantee, and duplicated store lines from a bad merge or rotation, caught at replay. 'Vacuous' overstates it.

Is the trace.md:84 guarantee misleading? Only a little. It promises immutability, and finalizeRecord honors a record_id supplied in the draft, which writeRecords then rejects as a duplicate, so immutability is enforced. It never promises idempotency. Is the existing assertion superficial? Partly. `expect(dup[0].validation.fail.join()).toMatch(/duplicate/)` at lib.test.mjs:146 is real for the same-id path, but the two writes share the same NOW, so a retry at a later time is never exercised.

Would the proposed test fail on the bug? Yes. Probe A (clock advanced 1 s) returns validation 'pass' and stored:true, so a test that expects refusal fails on current code. But the critic's suggestion to *change* the existing test would drop coverage of the same-id path (probes B and C). Keeping it and adding a new test is better, and the project rules forbid weakening tests.

How big is the impact? Bounded, as the critic says. latestByClaim keeps only the later duplicate. A CLEAR or other action attached to the earlier copy no longer counts toward consumerCoverage, because the copy is not superseded but is no longer the latest. records and byStatus are inflated. No fail-open licensing path was found: actionViolation still checks the status of each record.
repair:
Restated claim: TRACE-lite has no content-level idempotency. record_id hashes created_at (lib.mjs:234-238), and cli.mjs:109 stamps a new time on each call. So re-running `pnpm trace write` on a draft that was already stored, at a later millisecond, appends a second record for the same claim under a new id, and `pnpm trace lint` passes. The duplicate-id check itself works for same-batch duplicates, explicit reuse of a record_id, and duplicated store lines, so the immutability guarantee in trace.md:84 holds. The test 'append-only ... duplicates are refused' (lib.test.mjs:142-149) covers only the frozen-clock same-id path.

Bounded fix:
(1) Keep the existing test, renaming it to 'same record_id is refused' if desired.
(2) Add a new test that writes draft() at NOW and again at NOW+1 s and expects the second write to be refused as a duplicate (or as a no-op). This test fails on current code.
(3) In writeRecords, refuse a draft whose content, excluding created_at and record_id (and optionally provenance.branch), equals an existing non-superseded record with the same claim_id. Alternatively, derive record_id from that content key. Report it as 'duplicate content of <id> — write a revision instead'.
(4) Optionally add a lint warning (not an error, so existing stores stay valid) for two non-revising records with the same claim_id and identical content.

Severity: important at most, leaning nice-to-have. Immutability is not broken, and the only effect is duplicated or inflated records plus a skewed consumerCoverage.
reason: I confirmed the core mechanism by running it. Two CLI writes of the same draft 1.1 s apart both stored, got different ids, and passed lint with records:2. The unit test only passes because ctx() freezes NOW. The title's claim that the check is 'vacuous in real use' is refuted, though. Direct probes show the duplicate-id check does catch identical drafts in one batch, a draft that reuses an existing record_id (the real immutability guarantee in trace.md:84), and duplicated store lines at lint/replay. So the finding does not hold as stated. What holds is narrower: there is no idempotency for a retried write at a later time, and the test name implies more than it covers. Rewriting the existing test, as the critic recommends, would lose same-id coverage, so the repair keeps it and adds a new advancing-clock test. That new test fails on current code, as probe A showed. The critic's line citations are slightly off (213/218 should be 214/219, and cli.mjs:100 should be 109), but the content they point to is accurate.

claim_text: critic-panel lets the verdict-giver re-type a claim, which lowers the evidence bar, and the original type is not recorded
subject: the uncommitted TRACE-lite change set (see `git status` / `git diff`): scripts/trace/{lib,cli,bench-judge}.mjs and their tests, .claude/trace/schema-v1.json, the typed-verdict changes in .claude/workf

`applyEvidenceGate(v ? { ...v, claimType: v.claimType || t } : { claimType: t })`. The critic's type `t` is used only when the skeptic omits claimType, so the gate (:58-97, rule = EVIDENCE_POLICY[out.claimType]) checks the skeptic's type.
The returned object spreads `...f` and then overwrites `claimType: g.claimType`. The trace record sets `claim_type: o.claimType`. No field keeps the critic's original type.
semanticViolations checks accept against rec.claim_type, the already re-typed value, so `pnpm trace write` would not catch the downgrade either.

evidence.result: confirmed[0]: verdict accept, claimType factual, failedGates [], preGate accept; counts.confirmedBlockers 1, gateDowngrades 0. traceRecords[0]: claim_type factual, final_status accept, failed_gates []. The string 'measured' appears nowhere in the record (false).

evidence.result: No test covers re-typing. contracts.test.mjs only checks that the gate block is byte-identical and the roster has not drifted. It does not check how the call site picks the type.

evidence.ref: critic (qa-e2e): critic-panel.js:178 tells the skeptic to 're-type it if the critic mistyped it'. Line 281 passes `{ ...v, claimType: v.claimType || t }` into applyEvidenceGate, so the gate checks the skeptic's type, not the critic's. Stub run: a critic raised a `measured` blocker ('Bundle is over the 155 KB budget'). The skeptic returned verdict accept, claimType factual and evidence [{file_line page.tsx:1}]. Out

counter_reasons: Which path is uncovered? A skeptic re-typing a finding into a weaker claim type. scripts/trace/lib.test.mjs and contracts.test.mjs test applyEvidenceGate in isolation and check that it has not drifted. Neither runs the critic-panel call site, so the line-281 type choice is never exercised. Grep finds no retype test. The claim holds.

Is the existing assertion superficial? No test asserts anything about re-typing, so there is no assertion to quote. The only nearby check is the write-time semanticViolations (lib.mjs:190). It reads rec.claim_type, which is already the downgraded type, so it gives no protection. The claim holds.

Would the proposed test fail on the bug? Yes. My stub run of the real script shows the measured-to-factual re-type with file_line evidence ends as accept with failedGates []. A test expecting defer would fail today, so it targets the defect.

Is re-typing just intended design? Correcting a mistyped claim is intended (:178, :275), but the gate has no direction check. Any re-type, including one that lowers the bar, is silent. Because the original type is overwritten (:283 `claimType: g.claimType` after `...f`), neither the matrix nor the TRACE record can show the downgrade, and gateDowngrades counts 0. The overclaim is real and cannot be audited. The claim holds.

Is the recommendation sound as stated? Partly. 'Gate on the stricter of the two types' is not well-defined because EVIDENCE_POLICY is not totally ordered. For example, measured needs a measurement and normative needs a rule or human: neither is stricter. It would also block a legitimate correction, such as a missing aria-label wrongly typed as measured. A better-bounded fix: when the skeptic's type differs from the critic's, require evidence that meets the acceptNeeds of both types, or cap at the original type's onFail. evidence.ref: critic (qa-e2e): critic-panel.js:372 emits REUSE actions with the fixed note `still present on identical tree <treeId>`. lib.mjs:798-803 refuses any action whose contentKey (own id and created_at excluded) was already stored, and appendActions is all-or-nothing (:813-824). No. TREE_ID_EXCLUDES (lib.mjs:429-435) excludes .claude/memory/trace and the loop state files, so the tree id is stable and round 3 reuses the same record with the same note. This deliberate exclusion is also why the steady state of an L1 loop is plausible.

Refutation attempt 2: is the duplicate refusal for actions intended? It is, for decisions: lib.mjs:798 has the comment 'Same consumer decision twice … refuse it', and trace.md:120 documents it. Is the impact as strong as implied? No verdict is lost, because the reused record already exists. What is lost is bookkeeping (reuse metrics, the REAUDIT queue). The command also exits 1 on act --from, which a Lead following trace.md or loop.md may treat as blocking. For reaudit it is worse than the critic said: once any REAUDIT is stored, every later --act batch that contains it fails as a whole, so newly stale records are silently never queued, and the exit code is 0 (verified).

They share created_at, so action_id (a content hash that includes created_at) collides and replay reports 'duplicate id'. qualifier: The refusal applies from the second identical REUSE of a record on the same tree (round 3 or later), not to round 2's first reuse, which is stored. The loss is bookkeeping (REUSE/REAUDIT entries and metrics), not verdicts. The harm is that `act --from` exits 1, which the consumer protocol can read as blocking, and that `reaudit --act` exits 0 while silently dropping whole batches, including REAUDITs for newly stale records once any earlier REAUDIT exists. The fix should not just exempt these actions from the content-key check, because identical actions in one batch would then collide on action_id. Skip the duplicate as a reported no-op, or put a per-round discriminator in the note, and make reaudit --act exit non-zero when nothing is stored.

A mixed batch containing it drops a new REUSE because appendActions is all-or-nothing. On a copy of the committed store, `reaudit --act` stores 24 actions on the first run and 24 stored:false on the second, both with exit 0. I qualified rather than accepted for two reasons. The title says 'second round', but the first reuse (round 2) is stored and the refusal begins with the second reuse (round 3). And the consequence is lost bookkeeping plus a misleading exit code, not lost verdicts.

Does a union merge actually change that path's behavior? Yes, verified by command. Which existing test would catch it, and does it pass? None. All 93 trace tests pass and none exercise merge order. The committed-store replay test catches the bad store only after it is committed. GitHub's pull_request merge ref is base-first, so the PR's test job would go red before landing and that tool-only repair is still available. This assumes GitHub's merge honors merge=union, which neither the critic nor I verified. Only after a bad merge lands on the default branch do the repairs come down to a line reorder (a hand-edit) or a history rewrite. A revert followed by a re-revert replays the same tail-append, so it does not help. 'CI red permanently' and 'the only repair' therefore hold only for a merge that has landed.

Refutation attempt: does TR-780497ab3147 already cover this? No. Its union test only merged concurrent new appends and a CLEAR on a record from the same branch. It never covered an action on a pre-merge record whose claim the other branch revised. The gap is real.

Is the recommendation sound? Partly. Turning historical CLEAR/COMMIT violations in replay() into warnings would weaken the CI integrity gate for any action inserted out of band, and CLAUDE.md forbids weakening a safety gate. A safer order-independent repair is to evaluate the superseded and newer-record rules by created_at (the superseding record must predate the action) rather than by line position, which keeps genuine violations failing closed. (2) The recommended 'make replay() warn' fix would weaken the CI gate. evidence.result: git() wraps execFileSync in try/catch, sends stderr to 'ignore', and returns null on any failure

The result is {ok:true, checked:0, hits:[]} with exit 0 under a bad GIT_DIR, a corrupt index and a dubious-ownership refusal. The workflow's patch-text gate (loop-iteration.js:218-221) reduces the impact but does not refute the finding, because loop.md positions denylist-check as the catch for what that parser misses. Severity 'important' is appropriate.

claim_text: `denylist-check` inspects the whole dirty tree vs HEAD, so any pre-existing uncommitted `.claude/` or CLAUDE.md edit makes the loop revert and escalate an innocent patch
subject: the TRACE-lite machinery after the round-2 fixes (commit 7e3bd02; review the diff 8a999a3..7e3bd02 and the files it touches: scripts/trace/{lib,cli,bench-judge}.mjs and their tests, .claude/workflows/

evidence.result: denylist-check builds its path list from `git diff HEAD --name-status -z -M -C` plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`. That is the whole dirty tree against HEAD, not the paths in the applied patch. Only paths covered by TREE_ID_EXCLUDES are filtered out.
TREE_ID_EXCLUDES covers trace/, loop-plan.md, loop-run-log.md, log.md and quarantine.md. It does not cover .claude/memory/topics/*, .claude/memory/index.md or CLAUDE.md.
The production DENYLIST includes /(^|\/)\.claude(\/|$)/i and /(^|\/)CLAUDE\.md$/i, so any dirty wiki page or CLAUDE.md counts as a hit.

For an `applied` item the loop applies the diff, then runs `pnpm trace denylist-check`. A hit means 'revert, HOLD, escalate'. Nothing in the loop requires a clean tree first; step 3 only says 'Check git status'.
The post-apply denylist-check step is new in 7e3bd02. Before it, an applied patch was followed only by the smallest relevant check, so the claim that the old flow did not stall holds.

evidence.result: The before/after path-set difference was EMPTY, so a delta check would let the denylisted patch through. `git apply --numstat -z` listed .claude/memory/topics/tooling.md. Only the numstat option in the recommendation is safe.

evidence.ref: critic (regression): cli.mjs:171-172 lists every path that differs from HEAD (tracked diff + untracked), not the paths of the patch just applied; loop.md:109-111 says a hit means 'revert, HOLD, escalate'. Only TREE_ID_EXCLUDES paths are exempt (lib.mjs:437-443) - wiki topic pages and index.md are not. Scratch clone: `.claude/memory/topics/tooling.md` modified (what /dream ingest leaves behind; CLAUDE.md says never com

counter_reasons: Which caller depends on the changed code? .claude/loop.md:108-111, the `applied` branch of step 10 at L2/L3, runs `pnpm trace denylist-check` (scripts/trace/cli.mjs:168) after applying each patch and treats exit 1 as revert, HOLD, escalate. No other caller exists; loop-iteration.js:41 mentions the command only in an error message.

Does the diff change that path's behavior? Yes. 7e3bd02 added the post-apply check. Before it, a dirty .claude/ file had no effect on applying a patch. Now any uncommitted change outside TREE_ID_EXCLUDES under .claude/ or in CLAUDE.md fails the check. I reproduced the false positive on a patch that only touches src/app/page.tsx.
Which existing test would catch it? None. No test runs the denylist-check CLI subcommand (0 matches in cli.test.mjs and lib.test.mjs), and the 108 trace tests pass with the bug present.

Refutation attempt (is a dirty .claude/ tree realistic during a loop?): yes. CLAUDE.md asks for /dream after every non-trivial task, and /dream writes topics/*.md and index.md. CLAUDE.md also forbids committing unprompted, so these edits commonly stay uncommitted. TREE_ID_EXCLUDES leaves out log.md but not the topic pages /dream also writes. /improve-skills edits applied on confirmation and still uncommitted trigger it the same way.
Refutation attempt (is there a clean-tree precondition that prevents this?): no. loop.md step 3 says only 'Check git status and changed files', and loop-checklist.md says nothing about a clean tree.

Wording correction (does not weaken the claim): an escalated node is not ready, so the same node is not retried every iteration. Instead every node applied while the wiki edit stays uncommitted is escalated, which is the same stall.

Possible aggravation, not verified: loop.md says 'a hit → revert' without saying the patch. A Lead that tries to revert the reported hit could discard the human's uncommitted wiki edit, which would be data loss.

Possible aggravation, not verified: if isolation:'worktree' leaves an untracked nested worktree under .claude/ in the main checkout, `ls-files --others` would list it and every applied patch would hit. I could not confirm where worktrees are placed or when they are cleaned up.

Check of the recommendation: the primary fix, `git apply --numstat -z <patch>` before applying, is sound. It is still git deriving the paths, and I confirmed it reports the denylisted path. The fallback, 'snapshot the changed-path set and check only the delta', fails open: a patch that edits an already-dirty denylisted file adds no new path, and I measured an empty delta. Do not implement the path-set delta. The new test should cover both a pre-existing dirty .claude/ file plus an innocent patch (expect ok) and a patch touching an already-dirty .claude/ file (expect a hit).
reason: The claim holds as stated, and I confirmed it with commands. `pnpm trace denylist-check` (cli.mjs:168-180) checks every path that differs from HEAD, tracked or untracked, minus only the loop-state files in TREE_ID_EXCLUDES. An uncommitted .claude/memory/topics/*.md, index.md or CLAUDE.md edit, which /dream routinely leaves because commits happen only on request, therefore fails the check for any patch. In a scratch clone, a patch touching only src/app/page.tsx returned {ok:false, hits:[.claude/memory/topics/tooling.md]} with exit 1. loop.md:108-111 then reverts it, HOLDs it and escalates. The failure is a safe false positive, but it blocks every L2/L3 apply until a human resolves the dirty tree, and it is new in 7e3bd02. No existing test covers it; all 108 pass. For the fix, use the recommendation's primary option, deriving paths with `git apply --numstat -z <patch>` before applying. Do not use the fallback path-set delta: I showed it misses a patch that edits an already-dirty denylisted file. Add tests for both cases.

claim_text: F0 scan still fails open when the transcripts do not cover the runs: any single unrelated agent transcript lets `bench-score --record` store an `accept`
subject: the TRACE-lite machinery after the round-2 fixes (commit 7e3bd02; review the diff 8a999a3..7e3bd02 and the files it touches: scripts/trace/{lib,cli,bench-judge}.mjs and their tests, .claude/workflows/

evidence.result: The only fail-closed check on scan coverage is `if (flags.record && transcripts.length === 0)`. One transcript of any kind gets past it.

`contaminatedRuns(transcripts)` and then `markContaminated(runs, keys)` only mark runs whose agent transcript was scanned and leaked. `score.transcriptsScanned = transcripts.length` is reported and never compared with `runs.length`. The only other refusal is `score.unattributedLeaks`.
Labels are parsed only from transcripts that contain a leak marker. Nothing lists the runs that have no transcript at all.
`final_status` falls to `qualify` only when `contaminatedRuns || noVerdictRuns`. Otherwise it is `accept` with no qualifier. Scan coverage plays no part.

evidence.ref: node mkruns.mjs (22 verifier runs: 11 fixtures x 2 repeats, opaque tokens) + tx/agent-unrelated.jsonl with meta description 'some-other-agent'; node scripts/trace/cli.mjs bench-score runs.json --transcripts tx --record --store <scratch>/store.jsonl
evidence.result: exit=0; transcriptsScanned:1, contaminatedRuns:0, unattributedLeaks:0, no F0 flag (only 'F2 (informational)'); stored TR-e145ba8dd1f5 in the scratch store with final_status accept and qualifier undefined. 21 of the 22 runs had no transcript scanned.

evidence.ref: git show 7e3bd02 -- scripts/trace/cli.mjs; records.jsonl TR-ff5334ae3747 + HOLD action
evidence.result: The earlier round-2 fix closed the empty-dir and unattributable-label cases, which is consistent with the finding's framing. Coverage of runs by transcripts was never added.

evidence.ref: critic (regression): cli.mjs:413 only rejects `transcripts.length === 0`; nothing compares the scanned transcripts with the runs being recorded (score.transcriptsScanned is merely reported). Repro with a scratch store (`--store`): 22 verifier runs (11 fixtures x 2 repeats, opaque tokens) in runs.json and a transcripts dir holding ONE unrelated `agent-unrelated.jsonl` (+ meta description 'some-other-agent') -> `node sc

counter_reasons: Which caller depends on this code: /bench-checkers step 4 (.claude/commands/bench-checkers.md:38-43) runs `pnpm trace bench-score ... --transcripts <dir> --record` and treats `--transcripts` as the guarantee that 'an unscanned run is not a measurement'. The record goes through benchRecordDraft (lib.mjs:1086) into claim bench:trace-bench-lite, which gates the L3 loop. So the fail-open path feeds a durable `accept` measured record.

Does the code actually change that path's behaviour: yes, it fails open. The scratch-store reproduction stored an `accept` with no qualifier while 21 of 22 runs' agents were never scanned (exit 0, transcriptsScanned:1).

Which existing test would catch it, and does it pass: none would. cli.test.mjs passes 15/15, and its only bench-score test covers the missing flag. The record-blocking behaviour for a partial transcript set has no test.

Refutation attempt 1: in the normal workflow the transcript dir holds every agent's transcript, so this cannot happen in practice. This is partly true, but the CLI accepts any dir, and also a comma-list of dirs. Passing a wrong, stale, or partial dir (a different workflow run, or a dir where some agent transcripts were not written) passes the check silently. A fail-closed gate is meant to hold under exactly that operator error, and the earlier empty-dir fix shows the project already treats this class as in scope.

Refutation attempt 2: maybe some other check (unattributedLeaks, F0 flags, record validation) catches it. It does not. The unrelated transcript has no leak marker, so contaminatedRuns returns no keys, unattributedLeaks is 0, no F0 flag is raised, and validation passes.

Refutation attempt 3: maybe transcriptsScanned in the record evidence exposes the gap. It does not. The evidence `result` JSON in benchRecordDraft includes arms, externalJudgeGap counts and contaminatedRuns, but not transcriptsScanned, so the stored record does not show that coverage was partial.
Side note, not part of the verdict: bench-score stdout prints real fixture ids in externalJudgeGap. That is existing behaviour and outside this finding.
reason: The finding holds as stated. I checked it in the code and reproduced it. cli.mjs:413 refuses --record only when zero transcripts are found, and nothing compares the scanned transcripts with the runs being recorded. With 22 opaque-token verifier runs and one unrelated agent transcript, `bench-score --record --store <scratch>` exited 0 and stored TR-e145ba8dd1f5 as final_status accept with no qualifier and no F0 flag (transcriptsScanned:1, contaminatedRuns:0, unattributedLeaks:0). No existing CLI test covers a partial transcript set, and all 15 pass. The recommended fix is reasonable: derive the expected labels from the runs using the same regexes as contaminatedRuns, then refuse to record or force a qualify plus an F0 flag when any run is unscanned, and add a CLI test for a partial set. Important severity is justified because the gap writes a durable `accept` measured record that the L3 gate relies on.
